biography: Aamir Khan Productions was founded by Aamir Khan in 1999 and launched with Lagaan (2001), a then-unprecedentedly expensive cricket epic nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. The company became the vehicle for Aamir's selective, message-led career. He directed Taare Zameen Par (2007) for it, and it backed first-time or early-career directors including Abbas Tyrewala (Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na), Kiran Rao (Dhobi Ghat, Laapataa Ladies), Abhinay Deo (Delhi Belly) and Advait Chandan (Secret Superstar, Laal Singh Chaddha). Many productions were made with partners, among them PVR, UTV, Excel Entertainment, Disney, Zee Studios, Paramount and Viacom18, and Jio Studios. Dangal (2016), co-produced with Disney, became the highest-grossing Indian film and, with Secret Superstar (2017), is credited with opening China to Indian cinema. The banner's recent run is mixed: the costly Laal Singh Chaddha (2022) was a box-office disaster, while Sitaare Zameen Par (2025) was a hit and Lahore 1947, released in 2026 as Batwara 1947, was not. Of its films, ten feature Aamir Khan on screen, from lead roles to a cameo in Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos.

biography: A. R. Rahman was born Arunachalam Shekhar Dileep Kumar in 1967, the son of Malayalam film composer R. K. Shekhar, and made his name composing advertising jingles before Mani Ratnam's Roja (1992) launched his film career. Bombay (1995) sold 15 million soundtrack copies, and Ram Gopal Varma's Rangeela (1995) was his Hindi breakthrough and his first film with Aamir Khan; it won him the Filmfare Best Music Director award. His music blends Carnatic, Hindustani, Western classical and qawwali influences with state-of-the-art production. The partnership with Aamir continued through Deepa Mehta's Earth, then Lagaan (2001), whose songs won the Filmfare and National Film Awards for music and whose lyricist Javed Akhtar also won both. Rahman scored Mangal Pandey: The Rising (2005) and Rang De Basanti (2006), winning another Filmfare award for the latter, and Ghajini (2008), the first Hindi film to cross ₹100 crore nett in India, whose soundtrack was the year's best-selling Bollywood album. His international career peaked with Slumdog Millionaire, which brought two Academy Awards and two Grammys. He has seven National Film Awards and received the Padma Shri in 2000 and the Padma Bhushan in 2010. Across six films he supplied the sound of Aamir Khan's move from romantic hero to epic and political roles.

biography: Anand and Milind Srivastava are brothers and the sons of the veteran composer Chitragupt. Working as Anand–Milind from 1983, they debuted with Ab Ayega Mazaa (1984) and scored Jalwa (1987) before their breakthrough with Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988). Its songs, including 'Papa Kehte Hain' and 'Ae Mere Humsafar', won them the Filmfare Best Music Director award and helped make the film a phenomenon. The success tied them closely to the romantic cycle it started and to Aamir Khan's early stardom. Within two years they had scored Tum Mere Ho, Indra Kumar's Dil (a Filmfare nomination and the year's highest-grossing film), Deewana Mujh Sa Nahin and Jawani Zindabad, followed by Daulat Ki Jung (1992). Their collaborations with Majrooh Sultanpuri (QSQT, Tum Mere Ho, Daulat Ki Jung) and Sameer (Dil, Deewana Mujh Sa Nahin) supplied the courtship songs central to these films' appeal. Their long career includes more than 200 Hindi films, and in 2020 the Madhya Pradesh government gave them the Lata Mangeshkar Award. The fetched biography gives no birth years or detailed account of their style, so the stylistic description here draws on the film records.

biography: Bappi Lahiri was born Alokesh Aparesh Lahiri in Siliguri in 1952 to parents who were classical musicians; the singer Kishore Kumar was his maternal uncle. He scored his first film, the Bengali Daadu, in 1972 and gained recognition in Hindi cinema with Zakhmee (1975), produced by Tahir Hussain, before national success with Chalte Chalte (1976). In the 1980s he became the dominant sound of mass entertainers, introducing synthesised disco with Disco Dancer, Namak Halaal, Himmatwala and Sharaabi, which won him the Filmfare Best Music Director award. He set a Guinness record in 1986 for recording more than 180 songs in a year and composed across Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil and Marathi cinema. His work was also the subject of an international copyright case after portions of 'Thoda Resham Lagta Hai' appeared in a 2002 song by the American singer Truth Hurts. By the time he worked with Aamir Khan, the disco wave had peaked: he scored Love Love Love (1989), Dev Anand's Awwal Number (1990), Afsana Pyar Ka (1991), whose 'Tip Tip Tip Tip Baarish Shuru Ho Gayi' was a popular song, Isi Ka Naam Zindagi (1992) and Aatank Hi Aatank (1995). None became a major Aamir Khan hit. He received the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 2018 and died in Mumbai in 2022.

biography: Excel Entertainment was founded on 9 August 1999 by Farhan Akhtar and producer Ritesh Sidhwani. Its first film, Dil Chahta Hai (2001), starring Aamir Khan, Saif Ali Khan and Akshaye Khanna, won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi, and the company became associated with contemporary urban storytelling through Lakshya, Don, Rock On!!, Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara and Gully Boy, India's Academy Award entry. It later moved into streaming series with Inside Edge, Mirzapur and Made in Heaven. Aamir Khan's work with the banner covers leading roles in Dil Chahta Hai and in Talaash (2012), co-produced with Aamir Khan Productions; appearances as himself in Luck by Chance (2009) and, among many stars, in a song of the anthology Bombay Talkies (2013); and the narrating voice of the dog Pluto in Dil Dhadakne Do (2015).

biography: Kiran Rao was born in Bangalore in 1973 and grew up in Calcutta. She studied economics at Sophia College and mass communication at Jamia Millia Islamia's AJK Mass Communication Research Centre before working as an assistant director on Lagaan, where she met Aamir Khan, and on Mira Nair's Monsoon Wedding and Ashutosh Gowariker's Swades. She also appears briefly in Dil Chahta Hai. She married Aamir Khan in December 2005; their son Azad was born in 2011, and they divorced in July 2021 while continuing to work together. At Aamir Khan Productions she was associate producer on Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na and producer of Peepli Live, Delhi Belly, Talaash, Dangal, Secret Superstar and Laal Singh Chaddha. Her directorial debut, Dhobi Ghat (2011), which she wrote, follows four Mumbai lives, with Aamir as Arun, a reclusive painter haunted by a former tenant's video diaries. It premiered at the Toronto festival, drew strong reviews and was longlisted for a BAFTA. Her second feature, Laapataa Ladies (2024), was India's entry for the 97th Academy Awards. She has chaired the Mumbai Film Festival since 2015 and co-founded the non-profit Paani Foundation in 2016.

biography: Shankar Mahadevan, Ehsaan Noorani and Loy Mendonsa came from Mumbai's rock, blues, jazz and pop scene. Ehsaan and Loy began working together around 1989 composing advertising jingles, and Shankar joined them through composer Ranjit Barot. Their first film, Mukul Anand's Dus, was left incomplete after the director's death; Mission Kashmir (2000) brought them into the mainstream. Their breakthrough was Farhan Akhtar's Dil Chahta Hai (2001), with Aamir Khan, whose songs won them Filmfare's R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent and became part of the film's cult status. The trio fuse Shankar's Carnatic and Hindustani vocals with Ehsaan's rock guitar and Loy's electronic arrangement, a mix Gulzar called 'a sensible synthesis of popularity and class'. They won the National Film Award for Kal Ho Naa Ho and Filmfare awards for Bunty Aur Babli and 2 States. With Aamir Khan they also scored Taare Zameen Par (2007), whose song 'Maa', sung by Shankar Mahadevan, won National Film Awards for playback and lyrics, as well as Luck by Chance, Dil Dhadakne Do and, nearly two decades after TZP, the songs of Sitaare Zameen Par (2025). Shankar Mahadevan received the Padma Shri in 2019.

biography: Aditya Chopra wrote his first screenplays for his father's Parampara (1993) — in which Aamir Khan has a co-lead — and his mother's production Aaina, then directed Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995) and took over Yash Raj Films, which he has made the largest Hindi studio. His Aamir Khan films came under YRF: Kunal Kohli's Fanaa (2006), with Khan as a charming tour guide who is secretly a militant, was a major commercial success; Dhoom 3 (2013), which Chopra co-wrote, cast Khan as twin circus performers turned thieves and was one of the highest-grossing Hindi films ever made; and Thugs of Hindostan (2018), a period adventure with Khan and Amitabh Bachchan, opened to a record but was a commercial failure. He is notably publicity-shy despite his influence.

biography: Anu Malik, born in 1960, is the son of composer Sardar Malik. He composed his first film song as a teenager for Hunterwali 77 (1975), scored his first full soundtrack with Poonam (1981) and broke through with Mard (1985). Baazigar (1993) established him among the top music directors and won him a Filmfare award. His output combined melodious, classically inflected tunes with dance numbers, alongside repeated accusations of plagiarism. His four films with Aamir Khan came at the height of his popularity. He composed the songs for Ashutosh Gowariker's Baazi (1995) and Mansoor Khan's musical Akele Hum Akele Tum (1995), in which Aamir played an aspiring playback singer; the soundtrack sold about 2.5 million units and 'Raja Ko Rani Se' earned several Filmfare nominations. His songs for Indra Kumar's Ishq (1997) sold about 3 million units, and he was one of three composers on Dharmesh Darshan's Mela (2000). Malik later won the National Film Award for Refugee (2000) and a second Filmfare award for Main Hoon Na (2004), and judged Indian Idol from 2004 to 2018.

biography: Farhan Akhtar, born in 1974, is the son of Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani and the brother of director Zoya Akhtar. He apprenticed on Yash Chopra's Lamhe at 17, assisted on Himalay Putra and spent about three years in advertising before founding Excel Entertainment with Ritesh Sidhwani in 1999. His directorial debut, Dil Chahta Hai (2001), which he also wrote, followed three affluent Mumbai friends; Aamir Khan played Akash, the flippant joker who falls for an engaged woman. It was acclaimed for its realistic depiction of urban youth, won the National Film Award for Best Hindi Film and seven Filmfare awards, including Best Screenplay for Akhtar, and is credited with launching a new wave of urban Hindi cinema. Akhtar went on to direct Lakshya and the Don films, and to act, beginning with Rock On!! (2008) and winning the Filmfare Best Actor award for Bhaag Milkha Bhaag. As producer he backed three more projects with Aamir: Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (2009), in which Aamir appears as himself; Reema Kagti's Talaash (2012), co-produced with Aamir Khan Productions and with dialogue by Akhtar; and Dil Dhadakne Do (2015), where Aamir voices the narrating dog and Akhtar wrote the dialogue and appears on screen.

biography: Jatin and Lalit Pandit, nephews of the classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj and brothers of actresses Sulakshana and Vijayta Pandit, began composing together with Yaara Dildara (1991). Their breakthrough was Mansoor Khan's Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992), whose 'Pehla Nasha' brought their first Filmfare nomination and became one of the defining romantic songs of Aamir Khan's early career. In the following decade they scored landmark soundtracks including Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, with melodious compositions influenced by R. D. Burman. Their further collaborations with Aamir cover his changing roles: Ghulam (1998), including the playful 'Aati Kya Khandala', sung by Aamir himself and nominated for Filmfare Best Male Playback; Sarfarosh (1999), with 'Is Deewane Ladke Ko' and 'Jo Haal Dil Ka'; and Fanaa (2006), whose songs and Filmfare Best Music Director nomination came in the duo's final year. Despite their popularity they hold the record for most Filmfare nominations without a win. The brothers split in 2006 for personal reasons and reunited for a concert in February 2020. Their brother-in-law Aadesh Shrivastava composed the background score of Baazi.

biography: Nadeem Akhtar Saifi and Shravan Kumar Rathod met in 1973 and began composing together with the Bhojpuri film Dangal (1977) and the Hindi Maine Jeena Seekh Liya (1981). Their breakthrough came with Aashiqui (1990), given to them by T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar; its soundtrack sold 20 million units, reported as the best-selling Bollywood album of all time. Through the 1990s they dominated romantic film music with Saajan, Deewana, Pardes and Dhadkan, blending Hindustani classical colours such as bansuri, sitar and shehnai with filmi-ghazal melody, and won four Filmfare Best Music Director awards. Their collaborations with Aamir Khan began with Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin (1991), whose title song won Anuradha Paudwal a Filmfare award, and continued with Damini (1993), in which Aamir makes a cameo, and Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993). Their peak with him was Raja Hindustani (1996): its songs, including 'Pardesi Pardesi', won the Filmfare and Screen music awards, and the album sold 11 million copies. After Gulshan Kumar's murder in 1997, police accused Nadeem of involvement; he was exonerated by four courts, including the House of Lords, and lived abroad, which disrupted the partnership. Shravan Rathod died in 2021.

creative_style: Song-driven popular entertainment; Yaadon Ki Baaraat is identified as the first masala film, and Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak set the template for 1990s musical romance.
major_awards: Filmfare Best Film and Best Screenplay (Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak); Filmfare Best Film (Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar); Filmfare Special Award (1996)
historical_importance: Described as a major trendsetter in Hindi cinema; Javed Akhtar rated him the most underrated producer-director of his generation.
relationship_with_actor: Uncle. Cast him as a child in Yaadon Ki Baaraat and produced and wrote the films that made him a star.
biography: Nasir Hussain was born in 1926 in Bhopal State and joined Filmistan as a writer in 1948, writing hits such as Anarkali, Munimji and Paying Guest. His directorial debut, Tumsa Nahin Dekha (1957), made Shammi Kapoor a star, and a run of musical romances followed, including Dil Deke Dekho and Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai. Under his own banner he made Caravan (1971) and Yaadon Ki Baaraat (1973), a lost-and-found family saga identified as the first quintessential masala film, and Hum Kisise Kum Naheen (1977). His later films as director failed, and his son Mansoor Khan took over the company. Together they reinvented the romantic musical with Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), which Nasir Hussain wrote and produced; it won the Filmfare awards for Best Film and Best Screenplay and set the template for Hindi romance in the 1990s. Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992) brought another Filmfare Best Film award. For Aamir Khan, his nephew, Nasir Hussain was a formative figure: the eight-year-old appeared as young Ratan in the title song of Yaadon Ki Baaraat, and fifteen years later he launched Aamir as a romantic lead. He also wrote dialogue for Akele Hum Akele Tum (1995). He died in Mumbai on 13 March 2002.

name: Neeraj Vora
career_background: A Gujarati writer, director, actor and composer, born in Bhuj and raised in Mumbai, the son of the classical musician Vinayak Rai Vora; he came up through Gujarati theatre and television.
debut: Worked on Ketan Mehta's Holi (1984), Aamir Khan's first adult screen role; made his mark as a writer on Rangeela (1995).
major_works: With Khan: Pehla Nasha (1993), Baazi (1995), Rangeela (1995), Mela (2000); he also acted opposite Khan in Mann (1999). Wider work: Hera Pheri, Phir Hera Pheri (director), Garam Masala, Bhool Bhulaiyaa.
recurring_themes: Comic dialogue and screenplay.
historical_importance: One of the principal comedy writers of 2000s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: One of Khan's more regular writers of the 1990s: Pehla Nasha (where Khan appears as himself, and Vora also composed songs), the action film Baazi, Ram Gopal Varma's blockbuster Rangeela, in which Khan plays the Bombay street hustler Munna, and Mela. His article says Khan cast him as an actor in Mann.
biography: Neeraj Vora worked on Ketan Mehta's Holi (1984), the film in which the teenage Aamir Khan made his first adult screen appearance, and later wrote four Khan films. The most important is Rangeela (1995), Ram Gopal Varma's musical about a street-smart ticket seller (Khan) who loses the girl he loves (Urmila Matondkar) to a film star, a blockbuster with an A. R. Rahman score; Vora also stepped in to play a small role when an actor was absent. He also wrote Ashutosh Gowariker's Pehla Nasha and Baazi and Dharmesh Darshan's Mela, and Khan cast him as an actor in Mann (1999). Vora went on to write the Hera Pheri films and direct Phir Hera Pheri, and died on 14 December 2017 after a long coma.

name: Ritesh Sidhwani
career_background: A Mumbai-born producer from a Sindhi family who co-founded Excel Entertainment with Farhan Akhtar.
debut: Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Excel's first production, which won a National Film Award.
major_works: With Khan: Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Luck by Chance (2009), Talaash (2012), Dil Dhadakne Do (2015). Wider work: Don, Fukrey, Gully Boy; the series Inside Edge, Mirzapur, Made in Heaven.
recurring_themes: Urban, writer-led films; later streaming series.
major_awards: National Film Award for Dil Chahta Hai; BAFTA for Boong (2025).
relationship_with_actor: Produced four films with Khan, starting with Dil Chahta Hai, the coming-of-age comedy about three friends that launched Excel. Luck by Chance has Khan as himself; Reema Kagti's thriller Talaash, with Khan as a grieving police inspector, was a hit; and Khan voices the narrator dog Pluto in Dil Dhadakne Do.
biography: Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar founded Excel Entertainment with Dil Chahta Hai (2001), in which Aamir Khan, Saif Ali Khan and Akshaye Khanna play three friends in modern, affluent Bombay; it won a National Award and changed the look of the Hindi urban film. Excel went on to produce Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (2009), with a Khan cameo as himself, Reema Kagti's Talaash (2012), a supernatural police thriller starring Khan, and Dil Dhadakne Do (2015), which Khan narrates in the voice of the family dog. Sidhwani later expanded Excel into streaming with Inside Edge and Mirzapur and won a BAFTA in 2025.

name: Robin Bhatt
career_background: Son of director Nanabhai Bhatt and Hemlata Bhatt; elder half-brother of Mahesh and Mukesh Bhatt.
debut: Aashiqui (1990).
major_works: Aashiqui (1990); Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin (1991); Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993); Baazigar (1993); Raja Hindustani (1996); Mela (2000); Koi Mil Gaya (2003); Krrish (2006); Omkara (2006); Krrish 3 (2013)
recurring_themes: Mainstream romance, family drama and later science-fiction franchises
major_awards: Filmfare Best Screenplay (Baazigar, 1994); nominations for Omkara, Koi Mil Gaya and Krrish; Lifetime Achievement Award, Jaipur International Film Festival (2019)
historical_importance: A prolific writer of about 66 films whose credits span the 1990s romance boom and the Krrish franchise.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote four Aamir Khan films and shared the screenplay credit on Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke with him.
biography: Robin Bhatt, born in 1946, is the son of director Nanabhai Bhatt and elder half-brother of Mahesh and Mukesh Bhatt. He began writing with Aashiqui (1990) and has about 66 film credits. His work with Aamir Khan runs through the actor's most commercial romantic phase: he co-wrote Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin (1991), wrote the story and co-wrote the screenplay and dialogue of Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993) with Aamir, wrote the screenplay of Raja Hindustani (1996), which won him a Screen Award, and co-wrote the screenplay of Mela (2000). He won the Filmfare Best Screenplay award for Baazigar (1994) and was nominated for Koi Mil Gaya, Krrish and Omkara.

name: Zoya Akhtar
career_background: Daughter of Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani; trained at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts and assisted Mira Nair, Tony Gerber and Dev Benegal.
debut: Luck by Chance (2009), which won the Filmfare Best Debut Director award.
major_works: Luck by Chance (2009); Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011); Talaash (2012, co-writer); Bombay Talkies (2013, segment); Dil Dhadakne Do (2015); Gully Boy (2019); Made in Heaven (2019–2023); The Archies (2023)
recurring_themes: Privileged families and friendships under strain; the film industry; class and aspiration
creative_style: Observational ensemble drama with wry humour, often co-written with Reema Kagti.
major_awards: Four Filmfare Awards including Best Debut Director (Luck by Chance) and Best Director (Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara; Gully Boy); member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
historical_importance: One of the most influential contemporary Hindi filmmakers; Gully Boy was India's Academy Award entry.
relationship_with_actor: Four credits with Aamir Khan: his cameo in her debut, their co-written Talaash, the anthology whose song features him, and his narration in Dil Dhadakne Do.
biography: Zoya Akhtar was born in Mumbai in 1972 to Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani and is the sister of Farhan Akhtar. After a filmmaking diploma from NYU's Tisch School of the Arts she assisted Mira Nair, Tony Gerber and Dev Benegal. Her debut, Luck by Chance (2009), a critically acclaimed look at newcomers in Bollywood, features Aamir Khan among the industry figures playing themselves and won her the Filmfare Best Debut Director award. Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011) brought her the Filmfare Best Director award. With her regular writing partner Reema Kagti she co-wrote the story and screenplay of Talaash (2012), a neo-noir ghost story with Aamir Khan as a grieving police inspector. She directed the 'Sheila Ki Jawaani' segment of the centenary anthology Bombay Talkies (2013), whose song 'Apna Bombay Talkies' features Aamir among many stars, and directed Dil Dhadakne Do (2015), in which Aamir voices Pluto, the dog who narrates the Mehra family's cruise. Gully Boy (2019) won her a second Filmfare Best Director award and was India's Academy Award entry. With Kagti she founded Tiger Baby Films in 2015 and created the series Made in Heaven, and she later directed The Archies. She is a member of the Academy.

name: Ashutosh Gowariker
career_background: Born in Kolhapur; began as an actor in Holi (1984), where he met Aamir Khan, and worked in television and films such as Naam, Goonj and Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa.
debut: Directorial debut Pehla Nasha (1993); Baazi (1995) followed; both failed commercially. Breakthrough with Lagaan (2001).
major_works: Pehla Nasha (1993); Baazi (1995); Lagaan (2001); Swades (2004); Jodhaa Akbar (2008); Panipat (2019)
recurring_themes: Epic period and historical drama; rural India and national identity
creative_style: Long-form epics with large ensembles and music by A. R. Rahman.
major_awards: Academy Award nomination (Lagaan, as the film's director); Filmfare Best Film and Best Director (Lagaan; Jodhaa Akbar); National Film Awards; Academy voting member
historical_importance: Lagaan is India's third and, as of 2025, most recent nominee for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
relationship_with_actor: Friends since acting together in Holi; Gowariker directed Aamir in three films, and Aamir produced Lagaan.
biography: Ashutosh Gowariker was born in Kolhapur in 1964 and began as an actor, making his debut in Ketan Mehta's Holi (1984), where he met Aamir Khan, the start of a long professional relationship. He continued acting in television and in films such as Naam, Goonj, Chamatkar and Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa. His first two films as director both involved Aamir: the thriller Pehla Nasha (1993), a Body Double remake in which Aamir, Shah Rukh Khan and Saif Ali Khan appear as themselves, and the action film Baazi (1995), with Aamir as a framed police inspector; both failed commercially, and critics called Baazi a collage of Die Hard and Rambo. The partnership was vindicated by Lagaan (2001), which Aamir produced and starred in. The period cricket epic won the Filmfare Best Film and Best Director awards and eight National Film Awards, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. Gowariker went on to direct Swades with Shah Rukh Khan, the historical romance Jodhaa Akbar, which won the Filmfare Best Film and Best Director awards and was cited by the British Film Institute among the great Bollywood films of the century, and Panipat. He is a voting member of the Academy.

name: Indra Kumar
career_background: Worked as a producer before directing, with Mohabbat (1985) and Kasam (1988).
debut: Dil (1990), a major commercial success and the year's highest-grossing Hindi film.
major_works: Dil (1990); Beta (1992); Raja (1995); Ishq (1997); Mann (1999); Masti (2004); Dhamaal series (2007–2019); Total Dhamaal (2019)
recurring_themes: Family melodrama and romance in the 1990s; broad ensemble comedy later
creative_style: Crowd-pleasing melodrama built around hit soundtracks, later shifting to comedy franchises.
major_awards: Five Filmfare nominations, including Best Director for Beta and Raja
historical_importance: Delivered major romantic hits in the early 1990s and later popularised long-running Hindi comedy franchises.
relationship_with_actor: Directed three Aamir Khan films, beginning with Dil, the actor's biggest early hit after QSQT.
biography: Indra Kumar began as a producer with Mohabbat (1985) and Kasam (1988) before directing his first film, Dil (1990), under his banner Maruti International with Ashok Thakeria. Starring Aamir Khan and Madhuri Dixit as rival students who marry against their fathers' wishes, Dil became the highest-grossing Hindi film of the year, won Madhuri Dixit her first Filmfare Best Actress award and brought Aamir a Best Actor nomination. Indra Kumar consolidated his reputation with Beta (1992) and Raja (1995), both of which earned him Filmfare Best Director nominations. He reunited with Aamir on Ishq (1997), a broad romantic comedy pairing Aamir with Juhi Chawla and Ajay Devgn with Kajol against two scheming fathers; it was the third-highest-grossing Hindi film of 1997. Their third film, Mann (1999), a remake of An Affair to Remember with Manisha Koirala, is recorded inconsistently: the film's own Wikipedia article calls it profitable, while his biography calls it a commercial failure. After 2000 he moved decisively to ensemble comedy with Masti (2004) and the Dhamaal franchise, whose Total Dhamaal (2019) became his highest-grossing release. His three films with Aamir Khan span the class-conflict romance, the masala romantic comedy and the tearjerker.

name: Mansoor Khan
career_background: Son of Nasir Hussain; educated at IIT Bombay, Cornell University and MIT.
debut: Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), which won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and the Filmfare Best Director award.
major_works: Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988); Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992); Akele Hum Akele Tum (1995); Josh (2000); Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na (2008, co-producer)
recurring_themes: Youthful romance, coming of age, marriage and ambition
creative_style: Musical romances and Indian reworkings of Western films such as Breaking Away, Kramer vs. Kramer and West Side Story.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Popular Film and Filmfare Best Director (Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak)
historical_importance: His debut is credited with bringing back the musical romantic genre in Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Cousin. Directed Aamir Khan's breakthrough and two further films, and co-produced Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na with him.
biography: Mansoor Khan, born in 1958, is the son of filmmaker Nasir Hussain and a cousin of Aamir Khan. He studied at IIT Bombay, Cornell University and MIT before entering the family business. His directorial debut, Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), a tragic Romeo and Juliet-style romance produced and written by his father, launched Aamir Khan and Juhi Chawla. It is credited with reviving the musical romantic genre and won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and the Filmfare Best Director award. He reunited with Aamir on Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992), a campus cycling drama whose resemblance to Breaking Away was pointed out after release, and on Akele Hum Akele Tum (1995), a musical marriage drama loosely based on Kramer vs. Kramer. His last film as director, Josh (2000), drew on West Side Story; in 2008 he co-produced Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na with Aamir Khan. Across three films with Aamir, Mansoor Khan's work traces the actor's early persona from doomed teenage lover to underdog student to proud young husband. He later left the industry and settled in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, to farm, and has published The Third Curve (2013), on the world economy, and One: The Story of the Ultimate Myth (2023).

name: Nasir Hussain Films
career_background: The production company of the writer-director Nasir Hussain, Aamir Khan's uncle. It has no article of its own; this profile uses the article on Hussain.
major_works: With Khan: Yaadon Ki Baaraat (1973), Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992). Wider work: Teesri Manzil, Caravan, Hum Kisise Kum Naheen.
recurring_themes: Musical romance and masala entertainment.
historical_importance: Hussain's films set the template for the 1970s masala film and the 1990s musical romance.
relationship_with_actor: The family banner that started Khan's career: his first screen appearance as a child in Yaadon Ki Baaraat; his lead debut in Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, a blockbuster directed by his cousin Mansoor Khan; and the college sports drama Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar.
biography: Nasir Hussain Films was the company of Nasir Hussain, the writer-director of Tumsa Nahin Dekha, Teesri Manzil and Caravan, whose Yaadon Ki Baaraat (1973) helped create the masala film and whose production Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988) defined the musical romance of the following decade. Hussain was the elder brother of Tahir Hussain, Aamir Khan's father, and his banner is where Khan began: as a child in Yaadon Ki Baaraat, then as the lead of Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, directed by Hussain's son Mansoor Khan, and in Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar (1992). This row cites Hussain's article because the company has none.

name: Pritam
career_background: Pritam Chakraborty studied sound recording at FTII and composed advertising jingles and television title tracks.
debut: Co-composed Tere Liye (2001) with Jeet Gannguli; solo debut Stumped (2003); breakthrough with Dhoom (2004).
major_works: Dhoom (2004); Gangster (2006); Jab We Met (2007); Life in a... Metro (2007); Barfi! (2012); Dhoom 3 (2013); Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016); Dangal (2016); Laal Singh Chaddha (2022); Brahmastra: Part One – Shiva (2022); Animal (2023)
recurring_themes: Chart-topping romantic and anthem songs for big-budget films
creative_style: Fusion of Indian classical influences with rock, Sufi and contemporary pop; has acknowledged early plagiarism mistakes.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction (70th National Film Awards); six Filmfare Best Music Director awards
historical_importance: One of contemporary Bollywood's most prolific and commercially successful composers, with more than 125 film scores.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for three of Aamir Khan's biggest productions of the 2010s–2020s.
biography: Pritam Chakraborty, born in 1971, studied sound recording at FTII and wrote jingles for brands such as Santro and McDonald's and television title tracks before co-composing Tere Liye (2001) with Jeet Gannguli. His breakthrough was Yash Raj's Dhoom (2004), whose title track became popular internationally, followed by Gangster, Jab We Met and Barfi!. His style fuses Indian classical colours with rock, Sufi and contemporary pop, and he has acknowledged that he made plagiarism mistakes early in his career. With Aamir Khan he composed the songs for Dhoom 3 (2013), extending the franchise's sound, and for Dangal (2016), whose earthy, lyric-driven songs by Amitabh Bhattacharya, such as 'Haanikaarak Bapu' and 'Dhaakad', won Screen and Mirchi awards. He then composed Laal Singh Chaddha (2022); its songs, including 'Tere Hawaale', earned several Filmfare nominations although the film failed. Pritam has won six Filmfare Best Music Director awards and a National Film Award at the 70th National Film Awards. Across three films he became the principal song composer of Aamir Khan's large-scale later productions.

name: Ram Sampath
career_background: Composed advertising jingles in Mumbai before moving into pop albums and film music.
debut: Film work includes Khakee (2004); breakthrough with Delhi Belly (2011).
major_works: Khakee (2004); Delhi Belly (2011); Talaash (2012); Satyamev Jayate (2012, television); Raees (2017); Laapataa Ladies (2024); Sitaare Zameen Par (2025, background score)
recurring_themes: Contemporary rock-inflected soundtracks and socially themed music
creative_style: Versatile composer moving between advertising, pop and film with contemporary rock elements.
major_awards: Filmfare Best Music Director and Best Background Score (Laapataa Ladies, 2025)
historical_importance: Won a landmark 2008 plagiarism case over Krazzy 4, an important precedent for composers' rights in India.
relationship_with_actor: Aamir Khan Productions' regular composer: Delhi Belly, Talaash, the Satyamev Jayate television show and the Sitaare Zameen Par score.
biography: Ram Sampath, born in 1977, began in Mumbai's advertising industry and moved into pop albums and films, including Khakee (2004). In 2008 he won a plagiarism case against the makers of Krazzy 4, a significant precedent for composers in India. His breakthrough came with Delhi Belly (2011), produced by Aamir Khan Productions, whose 'Bhaag D.K. Bose' became an internet sensation and controversy; Aamir appears in the film's closing-credits song. He scored Talaash (2012), the Aamir Khan Productions and Excel thriller starring Aamir, with lyrics by Javed Akhtar, and composed the music of Aamir's television series Satyamev Jayate, including its title track. After a break he returned with Laapataa Ladies, directed by Kiran Rao, which won him the Filmfare awards for Best Music Director and Best Background Score, and composed the background score for Sitaare Zameen Par (2025), whose songs are by Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy. His career is closely tied to Aamir Khan's production company in the 2010s and 2020s.

name: Surinder Sodhi
career_background: An Indian film-score composer, often credited as Surendra Sodhi.
major_works: With Khan: Raja Hindustani (1996), Ishq (1997), Mela (2000). Wider work: Deewana, Soldier, Baadshah, Hera Pheri, 23rd March 1931: Shaheed, Special 26.
recurring_themes: Background scores for commercial films.
relationship_with_actor: Background scores for three Khan films: Dharmesh Darshan's Raja Hindustani, an all-time blockbuster; Indra Kumar's Ishq, a success; and Darshan's Mela.
biography: Surinder Sodhi is a background-score composer for mainstream Hindi films, credited on Deewana, Soldier, Baadshah, Hera Pheri and Special 26. He scored three Aamir Khan films: Raja Hindustani (1996), the romance between a taxi driver and a rich girl that was one of the biggest hits of the decade; Ishq (1997), a comedy co-starring Ajay Devgn, Juhi Chawla and Kajol; and Mela (2000), Dharmesh Darshan's action film with Khan and his brother Faisal. His Wikipedia article is short.

name: Tahir Hussain
career_background: Born in Shahabad to a schoolteacher from a Pashtun zamindar family; younger brother and protégé of Nasir Hussain, who directed his first production.
debut: Producer of Caravan (1971); directorial debut Tum Mere Ho (1990).
major_works: Caravan (1971); Anamika; Madhosh (1974); Zakhmee (1975); Tum Mere Ho (1990); Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993)
recurring_themes: Mainstream romance and family entertainment
major_awards: Filmfare Best Film and a National Film Award Special Mention (as producer) for Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke
historical_importance: A mainstream producer of the 1970s–1990s best known as father of Aamir Khan and Faisal Khan.
relationship_with_actor: Father. Produced Madhosh, directed Tum Mere Ho and produced Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke, which Aamir co-wrote.
biography: Mohammad Tahir Hussain Khan was born in 1938 in Shahabad. His elder brother, the filmmaker Nasir Hussain, brought him into the industry by directing his first production, Caravan (1971), which became a big hit. As a producer he went on to make Anamika, Madhosh and Zakhmee, the last of which gave the composer Bappi Lahiri early recognition. He was the father of Nikhat Khan, Farhat Khan, Aamir Khan and Faisal Khan, and his productions intersect with Aamir Khan's career at three points. Madhosh (1974) features the child Aamir as the younger version of its lead. Tahir Hussain made his directorial debut with Tum Mere Ho (1990), a snake-charmer fantasy starring Aamir and Juhi Chawla that failed at the box office but later gained a so-bad-it's-good following. His biggest success with his son was Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993), directed by Mahesh Bhatt and co-written by Aamir; it won the Filmfare Best Film award and a National Film Award Special Mention shared by producer and director. He died in 2010. Much of this profile comes from a search-result summary rather than a fetched page, so dates and titles carry lower confidence.

name: Yash Raj Films
career_background: Founded by director Yash Chopra; led by Aditya Chopra, vice-chairman from 2010 and chairman after Yash Chopra's death in October 2012.

biography: Yash Raj Films was founded in 1970 by director Yash Chopra and is led by his son Aditya Chopra, vice-chairman from 2010 and chairman after Yash Chopra's death in October 2012. The studio is known for landmark romances such as Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and for action franchises including Dhoom and the spy universe begun with Ek Tha Tiger. Aamir Khan's association began before he worked for the banner: Yash Chopra directed him in Parampara (1993), produced by Firoz Nadiadwala. For YRF itself, Aditya and Yash Chopra produced Fanaa (2006), the first film shot at YRF Studios and a major success. Aditya Chopra then cast Aamir as the twin circus-performer thieves of Dhoom 3 (2013), which became the first Indian film to gross ₹500 crore worldwide, and as the con man Firangi in the period epic Thugs of Hindostan (2018), which set a record opening before collapsing commercially.

name: Abhijat Joshi
career_background: Playwright and professor of English at Otterbein University, Ohio, since 2003.
debut: Kareeb (1998) and Mission Kashmir (2000) for Vidhu Vinod Chopra.
major_works: Mission Kashmir (2000); Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006); 3 Idiots (2009); PK (2014); Sanju (2018); Shikara (2020); Dunki (2023)

biography: Abhijat Joshi, born in 1969, is a playwright and has taught English at Otterbein University in Ohio since 2003, writing Hindi films alongside his academic career. His screen credits began with Kareeb (1998) and Mission Kashmir (2000) for Vidhu Vinod Chopra, and include Eklavya: The Royal Guard, Broken Horses, Wazir and Shikara. He is best known as Rajkumar Hirani's co-writer: Lage Raho Munna Bhai won him the National Film Award for Best Screenplay, and their dialogue collaborations hold records at the IIFA Awards. With Hirani he co-wrote 3 Idiots (2009), sharing the Filmfare awards for Best Story, Screenplay and Dialogue, and PK (2014), sharing the Best Screenplay award; he is also credited on Nanban (2012), the Tamil remake of 3 Idiots. The partnership continued with Sanju (2018) and Dunki (2023).

name: Advait Chandan
career_background: Began in 2007 as third assistant director and assistant production manager on Taare Zameen Par; assistant, casting director and post-production supervisor on Dhobi Ghat.

biography: Advait Chandan came up inside Aamir Khan's production world. In 2007 he was third assistant director and assistant production manager on Taare Zameen Par, and on Kiran Rao's Dhobi Ghat he worked as an assistant, casting director and post-production supervisor. His biography's career section is flagged as needing more citations. biography: Ketan Mehta was born in 1952 in Navsari, Gujarat, and studied at the Film and Television Institute of India before making documentaries in Gujarat as a television producer for the Indian Space Research Organisation. His first feature, the Gujarati Bhavni Bhavai (1980), won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration and established him in the parallel-cinema movement. Holi (1984), a largely improvised drama about a student revolt in a college hostel, followed; it gave Aamir Khan, credited as Aamir Hussain, his first adult role alongside Naseeruddin Shah, Om Puri and the future director Ashutosh Gowariker. Mirch Masala (1985) was nominated for the Golden Prize at the Moscow festival, and he went on to make Maya Memsaab and the biopic Sardar, which won a National Film Award. His interest in comedy, satire, romance, violence and rebellion carried into Mangal Pandey: The Rising (2005), a large historical production with Aamir Khan as the sepoy who helped spark the 1857 rebellion. The film marked Aamir's return after four years away, earned him a Filmfare nomination and drew political protests over its depiction of Pandey. Later films include Rang Rasiya and Manjhi: The Mountain Man. He is married to actress Deepa Sahi, a producer of Mangal Pandey.

biography: Mahesh Bhatt was born in 1948 to director Nanabhai Bhatt and Shirin Mohammad Ali, and entered films as an assistant to Raj Khosla. He directed his first film, Manzilein Aur Bhi Hain, at 26, and made his name with the autobiographical Arth (1982) and Saaransh (1984), India's submission for the Academy Award. With his brother Mukesh he co-founded Vishesh Films in 1986–87, and in the 1990s he moved toward commercial romance with Aashiqui, Sadak and Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin (1991). That film, a remake of It Happened One Night, cast Aamir Khan as a jobless journalist opposite Mahesh's daughter Pooja Bhatt; its success boosted her career and its soundtrack was widely praised. Two years later Bhatt directed Aamir in Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke (1993), a Houseboat-inspired family romance for which Aamir co-wrote the screenplay and dialogue with Robin Bhatt. It won the Filmfare Best Film award and Best Actress for Juhi Chawla, and a National Film Award Special Mention for Bhatt and producer Tahir Hussain. Bhatt stopped directing after Kartoos (1999), continuing as a writer and producer; Vishesh Films produced hits such as Raaz and Murder. He has won five National Film Awards and four Filmfare awards.

biography: Rahul Dev Burman, born in 1939, was the son of the composer S. D. Burman. He debuted as a music director with Chhote Nawab (1961) and broke through with Nasir Hussain's Teesri Manzil (1966), a major hit. Over the next two decades he became the defining sound of youthful Hindi cinema, writing scores for Hare Rama Hare Krishna, Yaadon Ki Baaraat, Sholay and Hum Kisise Kum Naheen, often with lyricists Majrooh Sultanpuri, Anand Bakshi and Gulzar and singers Kishore Kumar, Asha Bhosle, Lata Mangeshkar and Mohammed Rafi. His style drew on Western, Latin, Oriental and Arabic music, and he experimented with electronic rock, disco-rock fusion and unconventional recording methods. He married Asha Bhosle in 1980. He won three Filmfare Best Music Director awards, the last posthumously for 1942: A Love Story, released in the year of his death in 1994. His connection to Aamir Khan is limited to the child roles: he composed Yaadon Ki Baaraat, whose title song features eight-year-old Aamir as young Ratan, and Madhosh (1974), where Aamir played the younger Raj. Both films used Majrooh Sultanpuri's lyrics.

biography: Rajkumar Hirani, born in 1962, studied film editing at FTII and built a career in advertising before editing Vidhu Vinod Chopra's Mission Kashmir (2000). Chopra produced his directorial debut, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003), which won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film, and its sequel Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006). Hirani edits all his own films and writes with Abhijat Joshi, blending social commentary with comedy and emotion. His first film with Aamir Khan, 3 Idiots (2009), loosely adapted from Chetan Bhagat's Five Point Someone, cast Aamir as Rancho, a brilliant student who defies an education system built on rote learning. It became the highest-grossing Indian film at the time, won six Filmfare awards including Best Director for Hirani, and influenced debates about education in India, China and South Korea. They reunited on PK (2014), a satire in which Aamir plays an alien questioning religious intermediaries; it drew protests from Hindu nationalist groups but became the first Indian film to gross more than ₹700 crore worldwide. Hirani later made Sanju and Dunki, and his partnership with Chopra ended after Sanju. His biography reports that a biopic of cricketer Lala Amarnath with Aamir Khan considered for the lead was in development as of 2025.

career_background: Son of filmmaker P. L. Santoshi; assistant director to Govind Nihalani on Vijeta (1982) and Ardh Satya (1983).
debut: Ghayal (1990), a blockbuster and critical success.
major_works: Ghayal (1990); Damini (1993); Andaz Apna Apna (1994); Barsaat (1995); Ghatak (1996); Pukar (2000); The Legend of Bhagat Singh (2002); Khakee (2004); Ajab Prem Ki Ghazab Kahani (2009)
recurring_themes: Women's rights (Damini, Lajja), national integration (Pukar), activism (Halla Bol); also broad comedy
creative_style: Socially conscious action and courtroom drama, with a single foray into absurdist comedy that became a cult classic.
major_awards: Three National Film Awards; six Filmfare Awards for direction, screenplay, dialogue and story

biography: Rajkumar Santoshi, born in 1956, is the son of filmmaker P. L. Santoshi and trained as an assistant to Govind Nihalani on Vijeta and Ardh Satya. His debut, Ghayal (1990), was a blockbuster and critical success, and Damini (1993), a legal drama regarded as a cult feminist film, is widely considered his best. Aamir Khan appears as himself in a song in Damini, promoting their next project. That project, Andaz Apna Apna (1994), paired Aamir with Salman Khan as rival fortune-hunters in an absurdist comedy of mistaken identities. It flopped on release and was nominated for four Filmfare awards, then became a cult classic, voted the second-best Bollywood comedy in an Indian Express poll and re-released in a 4K restoration in 2025. Santoshi went on to Barsaat, Ghatak, Pukar, The Legend of Bhagat Singh, Khakee and Ajab Prem Ki Ghazab Kahani, and has won three National Film Awards and six Filmfare awards. His films are known for socially conscious narratives about women's rights, national integration and activism. He later directed Lahore 1947, produced by Aamir Khan Productions and starring Sunny Deol; it was released in August 2026 as Batwara 1947, with Aamir credited as producer rather than performer.

name: Reema Kagti
career_background: Assistant director on Lagaan, Dil Chahta Hai and Lakshya; associated with Excel Entertainment since its inception.
debut: Honeymoon Travels Pvt. Ltd. (2007).
major_works: Honeymoon Travels Pvt. Ltd. (2007); Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011, co-writer); Talaash (2012); Dil Dhadakne Do (2015, co-writer); Gold (2018); Gully Boy (2019, co-writer); Made in Heaven (2019–); Dahaad (2023)

relationship_with_actor: Assistant director on two of his 2001 films; later directed and co-wrote Talaash and co-wrote Dil Dhadakne Do.
biography: Reema Kagti learned filmmaking as an assistant director on three of the key films of 2001–2004: Ashutosh Gowariker's Lagaan and Farhan Akhtar's Dil Chahta Hai, both starring Aamir Khan, and Lakshya. She has been associated with Excel Entertainment since its founding and made her directorial debut with Honeymoon Travels Pvt. Ltd. (2007). With Zoya Akhtar she became one of Hindi cinema's most successful screenwriting partnerships, co-writing Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara, Dil Dhadakne Do, in which Aamir voices the narrating dog, and Gully Boy. Her second feature, Talaash (2012), co-written with Akhtar and co-produced by Excel and Aamir Khan Productions, cast Aamir as a Mumbai police inspector grieving his drowned son while investigating a star's death that leads to a ghost story. It was critically acclaimed and a hit, though some critics found the twist derivative. Kagti went on to direct Gold (2018), co-found Tiger Baby Films with Zoya Akhtar in 2015 and create the series Made in Heaven and Dahaad. Her work with Aamir Khan runs from the sets of his 2001 films to one of his most interior later performances.

biography: Ronnie Screwvala, born in 1956, pioneered cable television in India in 1981 and built UTV Software Communications into a media group with partners including News Corp, Fox, Disney and Bloomberg. Its film arm, UTV Motion Pictures, produced prestige and commercial hits including Lakshya, Swades, Jodhaa Akbar and Barfi!. With Aamir Khan it co-produced Rang De Basanti (2006) with director Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra; Screwvala shared its Filmfare Best Film award, National Film Award for Best Popular Film and BAFTA nomination. UTV also co-produced Delhi Belly (2011) with Aamir Khan Productions, and UTV Motion Pictures distributed Dangal in 2016. Screwvala sold UTV to Disney in 2012 and later founded RSVP Movies, which made Kedarnath and Uri: The Surgical Strike.

biography: Sanjay Chhel wrote one-act plays in Gujarati and television serials such as Nukkad before his first film, Pehla Nasha (1993), which includes a cameo by Aamir Khan as himself. He then wrote for Ram Gopal Varma's Rangeela (1995), whose colloquial Bombay dialogue for Khan's character Munna was part of its appeal; the film was a blockbuster. Chhel went on to write Kachche Dhaage and Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani and to direct Khoobsurat and Kyaa Dil Ne Kahaa.

biography: Shantanu Moitra, born in 1968, began in advertising, writing jingles such as the Uncle Chipps campaign, and composed Indipop albums including Ab Ke Saawan with singer Shubha Mudgal. He moved to Mumbai in 2002 to score Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi, and his songs for Parineeta (2005) won the Filmfare R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent. His association with Rajkumar Hirani began with Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006) and continued with 3 Idiots (2009), for which he composed the songs and co-composed the background score. With Swanand Kirkire's lyrics, songs such as 'Zoobi Doobi' and 'All Izz Well' became hugely popular, and the score won the IIFA award. He was one of three song composers on PK (2014), whose background score was by Sanjay Wandrekar and Atul Raninga. Beyond these films, Moitra scored Madras Cafe, Pink and October, won the National Film Award for the background score of the Telugu Na Bangaaru Talli and the Filmfare Best Background Score award for Sardar Udham. His restrained, melody-driven work kept the emotional register of Aamir Khan's two biggest comedies warm rather than broad.

He founded Vinod Chopra Films in 1985 and directed Parinda, 1942: A Love Story and Mission Kashmir. As a producer he backed all five of Rajkumar Hirani's films through Sanju. For Aamir Khan he produced 3 Idiots (2009), sharing its Filmfare Best Screenplay credit and the National Film Award for Best Popular Film, and co-produced PK (2014) with Rajkumar Hirani Films. He has won five National Film Awards and ten Filmfare awards.

name: Vijay Krishna Acharya

biography: Vijay Krishna Acharya, from Kanpur, studied at Kirori Mal College and entered films as the screenwriter and dialogue writer of Yash Raj Films' Dhoom (2004) and Dhoom 2 (2006). His directorial debut, Tashan (2008), opened to negative reviews. Aditya Chopra nevertheless gave him Dhoom 3 (2013), which Acharya wrote and directed, with Aamir Khan in a double role as twin circus performers robbing the Chicago bank that ruined their father. The film grossed about ₹400 crore worldwide in ten days, became the first Indian film to pass ₹500 crore and won the inaugural Telstra People's Choice Award at the Indian Film Festival of Melbourne, though Indian reviews were mixed. Acharya and Aamir reunited on Thugs of Hindostan (2018), which Acharya wrote and directed, with Aamir as the double-crossing con man Firangi Mallah opposite Amitabh Bachchan. It had the biggest opening day for a Hindi film to that point but was widely panned in India, criticised for its direction, writing and length, and became an expensive disappointment. The contrasting fortunes of these two films bracket the most commercially extreme stretch of Aamir Khan's later career.

biography: Vinod Chopra Films was founded by Vidhu Vinod Chopra in 1985 and became the home of Rajkumar Hirani's films. It produced 3 Idiots (2009), in which Aamir Khan plays Rancho, a free-thinking student at an engineering college, and PK (2014), in which he plays an alien stranded in Rajasthan who questions India's religious practices. Each became the highest-grossing Indian film on release.

biography: Vishesh Films was the Bhatt brothers' banner for more than three decades, producing music-driven romances and thrillers from Aashiqui to Murder and Aashiqui 2. It produced two Aamir Khan films: Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin (1991), Mahesh Bhatt's road comedy, and Ghulam (1998), Vikram Bhatt's On the Waterfront-influenced drama in which Khan plays a boxer drawn into a gang and sings 'Aati Kya Khandala' himself.

biography: Yash Chopra directed for more than half a century, from Dhool Ka Phool (1959) and Waqt to Deewaar, Silsila, Chandni and Veer-Zaara, and founded Yash Raj Films. Aamir Khan never had a lead role for him: Khan played one of the sons in Parampara (1993), a feuding-families drama with Sunil Dutt and Vinod Khanna that flopped, and Chopra produced Fanaa (2006), directed by Kunal Kohli, in which Khan plays a Kashmiri militant who romances a blind woman (Kajol). Chopra received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2001 and died on 21 October 2012.

biography: A. R. Murugadoss was born in 1974 in Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu, and trained as an assistant director on Ratchagan and on S. J. Surya's Kushi before his debut with Dheena (2001). Ramanaa (2002) and the Tamil Ghajini (2005), a revenge thriller about an amnesiac inspired by Memento, established him as a major action director. He remade Ghajini in Hindi in 2008, his Hindi debut, with Aamir Khan as the telecom tycoon who loses his short-term memory after witnessing his fiancée's murder. Aamir co-wrote the screenplay with Murugadoss. The film opened with record collections and became the first Hindi film to cross ₹100 crore nett in India, creating the industry's '100 crore club', though reviews were mixed about its length and violence. Murugadoss won the Producers Guild Best Director award. He returned to Tamil cinema with 7 Aum Arivu, Thuppakki, Kaththi, for which he won the Filmfare Best Director award (Tamil), and Sarkar, and made further Hindi films, Holiday (2014) and Sikandar (2025) with Salman Khan. His films typically wrap social issues into mass-market action.

He composed for over a hundred films and contributed songs to Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham. He wrote the background score for Baazi (1995), Ashutosh Gowariker's action film starring Aamir Khan as a police officer. Shrivastava, who was married to Vijayta Pandit, sister of Jatin–Lalit, died of cancer on 5 September 2015.

biography: Aditya Bhattacharya, born in 1965, comes from one of Hindi cinema's best-known film families: he is the son of director Basu Bhattacharya and writer Rinki Bhattacharya, and the grandson of Bimal Roy. He started out as an actor before turning to direction. His debut, Raakh (1989), co-written with Nuzhat Khan, is a stylish crime drama in which Aamir Khan plays a young man who turns vigilante after his girlfriend is raped by a crime boss, guided by a disillusioned policeman played by Pankaj Kapur. Shot before Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak but released after it, the film underperformed commercially but won three National Film Awards: Best Supporting Actor for Pankaj Kapur, Best Editing for A. Sreekar Prasad, and a Special Mention for Aamir Khan covering both his 1988–89 performances. Bhattacharya won the Bengal Film Journalists' Association award for Best Directorial Debut, and the film's photography marked Santosh Sivan's Bollywood debut. Raakh has since built a cult following. Bhattacharya's later films include Dubai Return (2005), with Irrfan Khan and Divya Dutta, which premiered at IFFI Goa, and Bombay's Most Wanted (2012). He divides his time between Barcelona and Mumbai.

biography: Deepa Mehta was born in Amritsar in 1950, grew up aware of the scars of Partition, and studied philosophy at Lady Shri Ram College before moving to Canada in 1973. There she co-founded Sunrise Films, directed television, and made her feature debut with Sam & Me (1991). Her Elements trilogy made her internationally known: Fire (1996), about two sisters-in-law in love, drew protests from Hindu fundamentalist groups; Water (2005), about child widows, had to be shot in Sri Lanka and was nominated for the Academy Award. Between them came Earth (1998), adapted from Bapsi Sidhwa's novel Ice Candy Man and seen through a young girl's eyes in 1947 Lahore. Aamir Khan plays Dil Navaz, the ice-candy seller whose rejected love for the nanny Shanta and the horror of Partition massacres turn him into her betrayer. Rediff called it probably the best performance of his life, and the film was India's submission for the Academy Award. Mehta's later work includes Bollywood/Hollywood, Heaven on Earth, Midnight's Children with Salman Rushdie and Funny Boy, which won the Canadian Screen Award for Best Director. She is an Officer of the Order of Canada. Earth is the only film in which Aamir Khan's romantic persona turns fully destructive.

Released in 1999, the thriller cast Aamir Khan as ACP Ajay Singh Rathod, a policeman whose family was shattered by terrorism, investigating an arms network run by his admired friend, Gulfam Hassan, played by Naseeruddin Shah. Filmfare's reviewer credited Matthan with drawing perfectly crafted performances from the whole cast, and Rediff praised the film for marrying serious and commercial cinema. Sarfarosh won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film, Filmfare's Critics' Award for Best Film and Best Screenplay for Matthan, and the Screen Award for Most Promising Debut Director. It also brought Aamir a Zee Cine Best Actor award. Matthan's later projects were slower: Shikhar (2005) was reworked after 9/11 made its brain-drain theme less relevant, and A New Love Ishtory, completed in 2009, was delayed until 2013. He chaired the feature-film jury at IFFI in 2021.

Kohli also wrote the dialogue. Released during a ban in Gujarat prompted by Aamir's remarks on the Narmada dam, it grossed ₹105.48 crore worldwide and marked Kajol's return after five years. It won Filmfare awards for Kajol, for lyricist Prasoon Joshi and for the singers of 'Chand Sifarish', though some critics found it melodramatic. Kohli's later films, Thoda Pyaar Thoda Magic and Teri Meri Kahaani, did not match its success, and he produced Break Ke Baad and made his acting debut in Phir Se....

biography: Nitesh Tiwari, born in 1973, graduated in metallurgical engineering from IIT Bombay in 1996 and worked as a creative director at the advertising agency Leo Burnett. His biography reports that Aamir Khan agreed to Dangal after its first narration, which it presents as a first in Aamir's career. Released in 2016 and written by Tiwari with Piyush Gupta, Shreyas Jain and Nikhil Mehrotra, the film tells the true story of wrestler Mahavir Singh Phogat, who trains his daughters Geeta and Babita into international champions. It won Filmfare Best Film, Best Director for Tiwari and Best Actor for Aamir, and became the highest-grossing Indian film, with extraordinary success in China. Critics praised its honesty while debating whether it truly centres the daughters or the father. Tiwari followed it with Chhichhore (2019), drawn from his IIT years, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi, and Bawaal (2023), and directed the two-part epic Ramayana. He is married to director Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari.

biography: Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra was born in Delhi in 1963 and studied commerce before working in sales for Eureka Forbes. In 1986 he founded Flicks Motion Picture Company and directed commercials for brands such as Coca-Cola and Pepsi. His first feature, the supernatural thriller Aks (2001) with Amitabh Bachchan, failed commercially. His second, Rang De Basanti (2006), was inspired partly by the Mandal Commission protests and follows a group of Delhi students cast in a British filmmaker's documentary about revolutionaries. Aamir Khan plays DJ, their charismatic, cynical leader, who is also cast as Chandrashekhar Azad. The film broke opening records, won the Filmfare awards for Best Film and Best Director, the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and a BAFTA nomination, and was India's Academy Award submission. Aamir won the Filmfare Best Actor (Critics) award. Its candlelight protests were copied in real life after the Jessica Lall verdict, and the media coined the term 'RDB effect' for such activism. Mehra later made Delhi-6, the Milkha Singh biopic Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (his second Filmfare Best Director award), Mirzya and Toofaan. He is married to P. S. Bharathi, who won the National and Filmfare editing awards for Rang De Basanti. In 2025 he chaired the international jury at IFFI.

biography: Ram Gopal Varma was born in Hyderabad in 1962, studied civil engineering and briefly worked as a site engineer before running a video rental store, where he studied which films audiences chose. After assisting on Telugu films he directed Siva (1989), a crime thriller that won Nandi Awards and introduced the Steadicam to Indian cinema. His Hindi breakthrough came with Rangeela (1995), a musical romance with Aamir Khan as Munna, a black-market ticket seller in love with his childhood friend Mili, played by Urmila Matondkar, who is being groomed for stardom. With A. R. Rahman's music and Manish Malhotra's costumes, the film was hailed for bringing a modern sensibility to mid-1990s Hindi cinema; it won Filmfare awards including Best Music Director and Best Story for Varma, and marked a turning point for both leads. Varma then redefined Hindi crime cinema with Satya (1998), Company (2002) and Sarkar (2005), pioneering a 'Mumbai noir' style, and scored a horror hit with Bhoot. His production 'factory' launched directors such as Anurag Kashyap and Madhur Bhandarkar. Rangeela remains his only film with Aamir Khan.

biography: Vikram Bhatt is the grandson of Vijay Bhatt, a pioneer of Indian cinema, and the son of cinematographer Pravin Bhatt. He entered films at 14, working with Mukul Anand on Kanoon Kya Karega (1982). His breakthrough came with Ghulam (1998), produced by Mukesh Bhatt and written by Anjum Rajabali from On the Waterfront. Aamir Khan plays Siddhu, an aimless Mumbai boxer drawn into a gangster's orbit through his brother, who finds the courage to testify and fight back. The film was a hit and earned Bhatt a Filmfare Best Director nomination. Its train-race dare won Filmfare's Best Scene award, and Aamir's own recording of 'Aati Kya Khandala' earned him a playback nomination. Bhatt then moved toward thrillers and horror with Kasoor and Raaz (2002), which earned a second Best Director nomination and began a franchise. Later films include 1920, Shaapit and Haunted – 3D (2011), which introduced stereoscopic 3D horror to India and became the highest-grossing Hindi horror film at the time. Ghulam remains his only film with Aamir Khan.
